author: pk910
content:
Your lib is a huge improvement when doing parallel hashing, so doing 1000 hashes in one go instead of doing 1000 sequentially is a huge win.
But going higher,  hashing 2000 instead of 1000 in one go doesn't give any measurable performance gain anymore.

Given that, I'm always hashing what I have in the buffer when exceeding 1000 pending hashes to gain some memory improvements instead. As storing all 1.x million validator hashes in memory is a big chunk too.

Talking about validators, there's a big  improvement possibility too:
Validators have 8 fields.  that's a power of 2 and therefore a complete tree without any zero leaves needed.
You can simply concatenate all Validator trees and collapse them in one go  instead of hashing each Validator (8 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1) individually.
That brought me far in front of the prysm htr performance when hashing big states 😉

The negative performance impact from progressive types are very small compared to these improvements.
